strict_linear.method: linear M-profile Thumb decode from segment start; stops at the first undecodable byte and deliberately does not resynchronise

recursive.method: narrow recursive M-profile Thumb walk from the v1.08 startup entries and hash-pinned callback targets; follows immediate BL/BLX calls and unconditional B only, not conditional edges or indirect calls/branches

whole_image_fpu_evidence.description: exact byte-literal occurrences of the CPACR and CPUID addresses anywhere in the decoded v1.08 application
whole_image_fpu_evidence.interpretation: No exact CPACR or CPUID address literal is present in the decoded application. This literal search does not exclude computed addresses, helper-mediated access, boot-stage configuration, or paths outside the instruction census.

esc2_dsp_windows.interpretation: The v1.08 application contains an address table and register-level transfer facility associated with ESC2 DSP program/data windows, plus IRAM/PRAM diagnostics. This supports a distinct DSP program/data control domain, but does not prove a separate CPU, physical memory map, amp-model ownership, or boot-time DSP load. Current traced callers are SysEx/control and diagnostic tests.

firmware_nam_signature_scan.description: byte-string scan of the decoded v1.08 application for NAM-specific container or engine signatures
firmware_nam_signature_scan.interpretation: No NAM-specific byte-string signatures were found. This does not rule out a generic model interpreter, nor does it show that one exists.

compute_bound.classification: conditional arithmetic from the published M7 benchmark and the board's 48 MHz CKCPU reference; not an ESC2 measurement
compute_bound.note: The 48 MHz CKCPU label is a board clock reference, not a verified post-PLL core clock. The MAC bound is a lower bound on the WaveNet weight work and ignores activations, head, resampling, and the rest of the effect chain.

conclusions.recovered_cpu: The inspected v1.08 application slices decode as Thumb/Thumb-2 integer code and include UDIV. No VFP/NEON or listed Armv7E-M DSP mnemonic was observed in the strict-linear prefix or narrow direct-edge walk. The prefix and direct-edge coverage are reported below; neither characterizes the full application or silicon.
conclusions.audio_domain: The application exposes a distinct ESC2 DSP program/data control domain through IRAM/PRAM diagnostics and transfer controls. It is not established whether this is a separate core, whether it executes amp algorithms, or whether firmware loads it at boot.
conclusions.nam_fit: This evidence does not establish native NAM fit or impossibility. The published optimized A2-Lite result is an M7 benchmark, not a GT-1 measurement; the board's 48 MHz CKCPU label is not a confirmed core clock. The DSP domain has no demonstrated compatible toolchain or amp-stage contract. No NAM-specific byte-string signature was found, which does not rule out a generic interpreter or a future port.
conclusions.practical_route: Host-side NAM can run over the GT-1 USB audio path as an external post-effect stage; it is not a firmware-level amp-stage replacement and the return is mixed at the final stage.

limitations: The strict-linear scan stops at the first undecodable halfword; its coverage and the direct-edge coverage are reported below. The direct-edge walk omits conditional branch edges, indirect calls/branches, and computed tables.
The strict-linear prefix contains BASEPRI/system instructions; a known SVC instruction occurs beyond its end. These findings do not characterize all system instructions in the segment.
This census covers only a prefix and narrow walk in one v1.08 startup-copied segment; the in-place code region at 0x60000000 and other copied segments were not exhaustively censused.
The in-place code region at 0x60000000 and other copied segments exist and were not exhaustively censused for FPU/DSP instructions.
Absence of exact CPACR/CPUID byte literals does not prove the silicon has no FPU or that no earlier boot stage configures it.
The 48 MHz CKCPU label is a board clock reference; the post-PLL core clock is not established.
The DSP windows are observed constants and strings, not a proven physical memory map, ISA, or audio call path.
No target benchmark was run; all cycle figures are upstream M7 references or arithmetic bounds.
